source_organization_or_authors: Ark Verma, Vivek Sikarwar, Himanshu Yadav, Ranjith Jaganathan, and Pawan Kumar; Language & Cognition Lab, IIT Kanpur

sources.title: Shabd: A Psycholinguistic Database for Hindi
sources.corpus_description: A 1.4-billion-token corpus drawn from electronic Hindi newspapers and news websites. The archive includes a frequency-sorted list of 96,122 forms occurring at least 100 times and a hand-screened database of about 34,000 words.

sources.title: KCIS Resources: Hindi tourism and health word frequency lists
sources.organization: Language Technologies Research Centre, IIIT Hyderabad
sources.funding_note: The resource page states that annotation was funded by KCIS, DeiTY, Government of India.
sources.license: No license or redistribution statement was displayed on the resource page at access time; only ranks and broad frequency agreement were used.

selection_procedure: Loaded the official Shabd v1.1 frequency-sorted 96,122-form list and reviewed the first 300 raw entries, exceeding the requested initial 150-200-item candidate review.
Compared plausible function words and high-frequency forms against both public IIIT Hyderabad KCIS Hindi word-frequency lists (tourism and health domains).

Kept high-frequency grammatical surface forms, including copulas, case markers, particles, auxiliaries, and common completed or habitual verb forms, because recognition of encountered Hindi is the deck's goal.

Extended beyond the news-heavy top ranks only when needed for indispensable beginner pronouns, question words, everyday verbs, adjectives, adverbs, and nouns; every retained form has a source rank recorded in the TSV.
Balanced the final 100 across function words, pronouns, question words, verbs and verb forms, modifiers, and everyday nouns, then assigned a learner-oriented final Frequency Rank from 1 through 100.
Wrote and reviewed every English gloss, grammar note, pronunciation, Hindi example, example pronunciation, and translation specifically for this deck.
exclusions: bare Arabic or Devanagari numeral tokens
Latin-script web and corpus artifacts such as com and jagran
proper names, surnames, place names, and political or highly news-specific named entities
exact duplicate forms in the Shabd database
specialist medical, administrative, crime, and election vocabulary unsuitable for a first 100-card learner set
redundant inflected variants when they would crowd out a more essential grammatical or everyday form
conflicting_rankings: No synthetic average was calculated across the very large Shabd newspaper corpus and the two small domain-specific IIIT lists. Shabd rank was preferred when the exact form was present. For short function words absent from the Shabd 96,122-form file, an exact IIIT rank was recorded. Cross-source agreement raised confidence; disagreement was resolved by beginner recognition value, grammatical coverage, and avoidance of news-domain distortion.

romanization_convention.name: IAST-influenced practical Hindi pronunciation
romanization_convention.long_vowels: ā, ī, and ū mark long vowels.
romanization_convention.retroflexes: ṭ, ḍ, and ṇ mark retroflex stops/nasals; ṛ marks the flap written ड़.
romanization_convention.aspiration: Aspiration is explicit: kh, gh, chh, jh, ṭh, ḍh, th, dh, ph, and bh.
romanization_convention.nasalization: A tilde on the pronounced vowel marks vowel nasalization, for example mẽ, maĩ, haĩ, and kahā̃.
romanization_convention.schwa_deletion: Pronunciations reflect standard modern Hindi schwa deletion, for example करना karnā, पहले pahle, देखना dekhnā, and रहना rahnā.
romanization_convention.sh_and_ssa: श and ष are both represented as sh in ordinary modern pronunciation; conjunct spellings are rendered for the spoken sequence, for example कक्षा kakshā.
romanization_convention.spoken_demonstratives: यह and वह are represented by their ordinary spoken pronunciations yeh and vo when used as pronouns or determiners.
romanization_convention.scope: This is learner-friendly pronunciation guidance, not strict phonemic transcription or IPA. The same conventions are used in Word and complete-sentence pronunciation fields.

independent_content_confirmation: All definitions, grammar notes, pronunciations, Hindi example sentences, sentence pronunciations, and English translations in hindi_core_100.tsv were independently written or curated for this deck. No corpus, dictionary, learner-site, audio, or proprietary editorial sentence was copied.
